The Prophet told an Ansari who was admonishing his brother about modesty to leave him, for modesty is part of faith.
Among the sayings of earlier prophets that people still have: if you do not feel ashamed, then do whatever you like.
Ibn Abbas said 'they fold up their breasts' concerned people too shy to relieve themselves or have relations with their wives in the open under the sky.
When the verse telling women to draw their veils over their bosoms came, the early emigrant women cut their garments and covered their heads and faces with them.
Umar urges veiling the Prophet's wives; guests lingering after the Prophet's wedding feast for Zainab lead to the verse of the screen, and women are allowed out for their needs.
Men must not enter upon women or be alone with one without a mahram, in-laws above all; the Prophet spoke aside with an Ansari woman and barred an effeminate man.
Aisha watched Ethiopians play, screened by the Prophet; women may go out for needs or to the mosque; foster uncles may enter; wives must not describe women to husbands.
Guests lingered after the Prophet's wedding meal for Zainab bint Jahsh; when they left he hung a curtain before Anas, and the verse of Hijab was revealed.
Haya, pious shyness, brings only good and is part of faith; the Prophet was shyer than a veiled virgin, yet Allah is not shy of the truth.
The Prophet turned Al-Fadl's face from a Khath'am woman asking about Hajj for her father, and told those sitting on roads to lower their gaze, harm none and return greetings.
